components.role: Normalizing flows are used to model expressive and multimodal posterior distributions, capture latent variability, or learn flexible distributions.
Density estimation provides data-generating or conditional densities that serve as the foundation for downstream probabilistic and clustering tasks.
Uncertainty quantification assesses epistemic and probabilistic uncertainty in complex models by leveraging posterior distributions or density estimates.

target_task.text: The combination targets tasks such as Bayesian causal discovery, generative shape modeling, and density-based clustering with associated uncertainty.

limitation.text: Existing approaches often fail to encode complex dependencies, lack principled ways to handle multimodal posteriors, or struggle to scale efficiently while providing rigorous inference.

combination.text: Normalizing flows are combined with density estimation to support expressive posterior learning, while density-based clustering or resampling schemes enable principled uncertainty quantification.
